觯: A drinking horn used at the village drinking ceremony. The ritual says: "One man washes and raises the 觶, which holds four pints." The [Yupian]: "It is a wine cup." The [Zengyun]: "When full it is called 觴, when empty 觶." The [Liji], 'Liqi': "The honored one raises the 觶." The commentary: "Three pints is called 觶; 觶 is 適, for one should drink in due measure."
觱: The horn blown by the Qiang people, called 屠觱, to startle horses. Xu says: "What is now the 觱栗; its sound is of that description." The popular form is 篳篥.
觳: A vessel for holding a 觵 or a wine cup; another account makes it an archery implement. The [Leipian]: "觳簏 is the name of a vessel."
觴: When a 觶 is full it is called 觴; when empty, 觶. The [Yunhui]: "It is the general name for a wine vessel." The [Sanli Tu]: "All 觴 are alike in form, though they differ in capacity." The sub-commentary to the [Shijing], 'Zhou Nan, Juan Er': "One pint is called 爵, two pints 觚, three pints 觶, four pints 角, five pints 散; the general name is 爵, and what it contains is called 觴. 觴 is 餉 (to present)." The [Zuo Zhuan], second year of Duke Cheng: "He presented the cup of wine with a jade disk and advanced." The [Qian Hanshu], 'Waiqi Zhuan': "Pour the feathered cup to dispel sorrow." Meng Kang says: "The feathered cup is a 爵 made in the shape of a living sparrow, with head, tail, and wings."
觸: To butt, to collide. The [Yijing], 'Dazhuang': "A ram butts against a hedge." The [Qian Hanshu], 'Annals of Emperor Yuan': "Casting off ritual and rightness, colliding — (the passage breaks off here)."
訁: "A straightforward statement is called 言; discussion and objection is called 語." The commentary to the [Zhouli], 'Dasile': "To begin a topic is 言; to answer and narrate is 語." The [Shiming]: "言 is 宣, to make known the meaning of each to the other." The [Yijing], 'Qian' hexagram: "The truthfulness of ordinary speech." The [Shujing], 'Tang Shi': "I will not eat my words." The commentary: "It means to have spoken and then to swallow one's words again." The [Zhouli], 'Diguan, Dasitu': "By the eight [headings] of the district — (the passage breaks off here)." The form 訁 is the abbreviated radical used as a component; no structural field is recorded in the source, and it is classified as a compound ideograph (会意).
计: To sum up, to reckon. It is composed of 言 and 十; Xu says: "Ten is the completed number of things" — a compound ideograph. The [Zuo Zhuan], thirty-second year of Duke Zhao: "Shi Mimou laid out Chengzhou and calculated its measurements." The [Liji], 'Nei Ze': "At ten years he goes out to a foreign tutor, resides away from home, and learns writing and calculation." The commentary: "Writing means the six scripts; calculation means the nine numbers." The [Zhouli], 'Tianguan': "The Junior Steward uses the six reckonings to decide the governance of the various officials." The commentary: "弊 means to judge; the six reckonings are goodness, ability, reverence, correctness, law, and discrimination, all rooted in integrity, and he weighs the amount of merit and fault and adjudicates accordingly."
订: To settle by discussion, to revise. The [Shijing], 'Zhousong': "He made it, and King Wen brought peace to it." The commentary: "By this he revised the ways of King Tai and King Wen, so that they stood out and matched the virtue of heaven and earth." The sub-commentary: "訂 means to compare — (the passage breaks off here)."

讥: To censure, to ridicule. The [Zengyun]: "To mock." The [Zuo Zhuan], first year of Duke Yin: "He called him 'the Earl of Zheng' to censure his failure to teach." Ban Gu's 'Dian Yin': "Sima Qian wrote his book with subtle words and piercing censure, disparaging his own age."
讦: To denounce a person face to face; to accuse one another. The [Yupian]: "To attack a person's private secrets." The [Guangyun]: "To reproach a person to his face." The [Lunyu]: "He hates those who take denunciation as uprightness." The [Qian Hanshu], 'Waiqi Zhuan': "To expose and broadcast hidden faults."
讧: Disorder, internal strife. The [Yupian]: "To collapse, to be defeated." The [Zengyun]: "Confusion." The [Shijing], 'Daya': "The 蟊 and the 賊 bring internal strife (內訌)." The commentary: "To collapse." The gloss: "Words of litigation that entrap others." The [Tangshu], 'Eulogy of Guo Ziyi': "Externally blocked, internally in strife."
讨: To regulate, to punish. It is composed of 言 and 寸; Xu says: "寸 is the measure of law; to bear a proclamation and punish crime, therefore it follows 言" — a compound ideograph. The [Shujing], 'Gaoyao Mo': "Heaven punishes the guilty." The sub-commentary: "To regulate and punish the guilty, so that they may be cut off from evil." The [Zuo Zhuan], twelfth year of Duke Xuan: "Their ruler never a day failed to review (討) the people of the state and instruct them." The commentary: "討 means to regulate."
让: To reprove; also to yield. The [Xiao Erya]: "To censure with words is called 讓." The [Zuo Zhuan], fifth year of Duke Xi: "The duke sent someone to reprove him." The commentary: "To reprimand and reprove him." The [Zhouli], 'Diguan': "The Superintendent of Rescue is in charge of the wickedness and faults of the myriad people and punishes and reproves them." The [Shiji], 'Biography of Zhang Er' — (the passage breaks off here).
讪: To slander, to deride. It is composed of 言 with 山 as phonetic. The [Yupian]: "Words of defamation." The [Liji], 'Shaoyi': "One who is a minister or subject may remonstrate but not deride." The [Lunyu]: "He hates those who, dwelling in low places, deride their superiors." The [Guan Yinzi], 'Jiu Yao' chapter: "One must not deride and slander those whose virtue is complete." Yang Xiong's [Fayan]: "Reckless praise is the enemy of benevolence; reckless defamation is the enemy of rightness. One who harms benevolence is near the 'village worthy'; one who harms rightness is near the village derider."
讫: To stop, to finish. Xu says: "The stopping of speech." The [Yupian]: "To be finished." The [Zengyun]: "To end, to be done." The [Zihui]: "To be exhausted." The [Shujing], 'Lü — (the passage breaks off here)."
讬: To entrust, to place with another. Yang Xiong's [Fangyan]: "In general, to entrust is 託." The [Yupian]: "To rely on." The [Zengyun]: "To commission; also to trust." The [Guliang Zhuan], first year of Duke Ding: "As for one who makes a request, he cannot go having merely entrusted it to another." Fan's commentary: "詒託 is like borrowing and entrusting." The [Liji], 'Tangong': "Long has it been since I lodged (託) my mind in music." Zheng's commentary: "To lodge." The [Qian Hanshu], 'Biography of Jia Shan': "They gathered and lodged together." The [Tangshu], 'Biography of Li Ji': "Li Ji being loyal and strong, the emperor said that great matters could be entrusted to him." The [Shuoyuan], 'Shan Shuo': "A superior man may be entrusted with beauty, a middling man with words, an inferior man with wealth."
训: To explain and teach. Xu says: "訓 means to instruct by following the sense." The [Zhengyun]: "To teach." The [Zihui]: "To guide." The [Shujing], 'Yi Xun': "Yi Yin then plainly set forth the accomplished virtue of the glorious ancestor to instruct the king." The commentary: "He made the 'Xun' to teach and guide Tai Jia." The [Shijing], 'Daya': "The four quarters are instructed by him." The Correct Meaning: "訓 is another name for teaching and instructing." The [Liji], 'Quli': "To teach and instruct and to correct customs." The sub-commentary: "It means to explain the principles of right."
议: To speak, to deliberate. Xu says: "To determine what is fitting in a matter." The [Guangya]: "To speak; to plan." The [Guangyun]: "To judge." The [Zhengyun]: "To discuss." The [Yijing], 'Jie' hexagram: "The gentleman accordingly institutes measures and degrees and deliberates on virtuous conduct." The [Shujing], 'Zhouguan': "They deliberate on affairs in order to institute them." The [Liji], 'Quli': "Public affairs are not deliberated in private." The [Zhuangzi], 'Qiwu Lun': "Within the six directions, the sage discusses but does not adjudicate." The [Wenzhongzi], 'Wen Yi' chapter: "Do they deliberate so as to exhaust the mind of the world?" The commentary: "The 'Xu Shu' contains deliberations."
讯: Structurally a left-right phono-semantic compound (形声). [note: source text partially corrupted]
记: To record, to note down separately. Xu says: "It means to record each one separately." The [Guangya]: "To know, to mark." The [Shiming]: "It is 紀 (a skein)." The [Yupian]: "To register." The [Guangyun]: "To set down." The [Shujing], 'Yi and Ji': "He struck them to make them remember." The commentary: "He caused them to record and remember their faults." The [Liji], 'Wangzhi': "The Grand Scribe presides over the rites and holds — (the passage breaks off here)."
讲: To reconcile, to make peace; to explain. Xu says: "The ancients spoke of 講解 in the sense of 和解 (reconciliation)." The [Zhanguo Ce]: "Now you forbid it, though Qin has not yet made peace with Wei."
讳: To avoid mentioning; to taboo. The [Guangyun]: "To avoid." The [Yupian]: "To conceal, to scruple." The preface to the [Chunqiu]: "To conceal and avoid, so as to escape harm." The [Gongyang Zhuan], first year of Duke Min: "The Chunqiu avoids names for the honored, avoids them for relatives, and avoids them for the worthy." The [Zhanguo Ce]: "In punishment it does not avoid the powerful." The commentary: "諱 is like avoiding." The [Shiji], 'Annals of the First Emperor of Qin': "Qin customs had many prohibitions of taboo."
讴: To sing in unison. The [Qian Hanshu], 'Annals of Emperor Gao': "When the King of Han had arrived at Nan Zheng, the generals and soldiers all sang and chanted, longing to return east." Shigu's commentary: "It means to sing in unison; some say it is a song of the land of Qi."
讵: 詎 is like 豈 (how could it be?). The [Zhuangzi], 'Dazongshi': "How could one know that what I call heaven is not man?" The [Hou Hanshu], 'Annals of Emperor Guangwu': "How can the world be known and yet one shut out the elders?" The [Songshu], 'Preface by Shen Yue': "If a single messenger galloped forth, how would the four quarters not respond?"
讶: To welcome, to meet a guest. It quotes the [Zhouli], 'Qiuguan': "Among the feudal lords there are those who have a minister to welcome guests (訝)." Xu says: "According to the [Zhouli], when an envoy was about to arrive, a minister was sent to welcome him — that is, to meet him with words and reassure him."
讷: Difficulty in speaking, slow of speech. The [Yupian]: "Slow and dull." The [Guangyun]: "Stammering." The [Lunyu]: "The gentleman wishes to be slow in speech and quick in action." The [Guan Yinzi], 'Jiu Yao' chapter: "He who exhausts the world's arguments relies not on argument but on reticence."
许: To allow, to consent to. The [Guangya]: "To give, to grant." The [Yupian]: "To follow, to agree." The [Guangyun]: "To permit." The [Zengyun]: "To agree and promise." The [Shujing], 'Jin Teng': "If you grant me, I shall return with the jade disk and tablet and await your command; if you do not grant me, I shall put away the jade disk and tablet." The [Shiji], 'Annals of Emperor Gaozu': "Old Lady Lü was angry. Lü Gong said: 'I have long wished to make this daughter a remarkable match with a noble man; why do you rashly promise her to Liu Ji?'"
讹: Structurally a left-right phono-semantic compound (形声). [note: source text partially corrupted]
论: To discuss. The [Guangyun]: "To speak of." Jia Gongyan's sub-commentary to the [Zhouli], 'Chunguan, Dasile': "A straightforward statement is 論; an answer to a difficulty is 語. 論 is a subdivision of speech and differs from 言."
讼: To sing, to praise; and by extension litigation. Xu Xuan says: "In the ancient text of the Mao Odes, the characters 雅 and 頌 are mostly written 訟."
讽: To recite, to exhort. The [Zhouli], 'Chunguan, Dasile': "By the language of music he taught the sons of the state, stirring them by recitation (諷), chanting, speech, and discourse." The commentary: "To recite from memory is 諷; to give it rhythm with the voice is 誦." The [Qian Hanshu], 'Yiwenzhi': "The Grand Scribe examined the students: those able to recite nine thousand characters or more from memory could become scribes." The [Jinshu], 'Biography of Ruan Zhan': "To recite the words of the departed is not as good as receiving the tone of their instruction in person."
设: Recorded only as a left-right compound ideograph (会意) in the source. [note: source text partially corrupted]
访: "To consult broadly is called 訪." Xu says: "This speaks of broad consultation, namely asking widely of people." The [Erya], 'Shi Gu': "To plan, to consult." The [Yupian]: "To ask." The [Shujing], 'Hongfan': "The king consulted Jizi." The commentary: "It means to go to him and question him." The [Zhouli], 'Chunguan': "He received and admitted consultations in order to inform the king in the conduct of government." The commentary: "To present counsels to the king."
诀: To part, to take leave. The [Zengyun]: "To say farewell." The [Shiji], 'Biography of Wu Qi': "He went out east through the gate of the outer wall of Wei and took leave of his mother." The [Hou Hanshu], 'Biography of Lei Yi': "He travelled lightly to wait upon him, in order to have a final parting."
证: Structurally a left-right phono-semantic compound (形声). [note: source text partially corrupted]
诂: To explain ancient words. It quotes the 'Guxun' of the [Shijing]; Kong Yingda's sub-commentary: "詁, 訓, and 傳 are other names for commentary: 詁 means that the words of ancient and modern times differ, and one makes them understood." Xu says: "According to the [Erya], 詁 means ancient, for speech has its ancient and modern forms" — a compound ideograph. The [Guangya]: "Words." The [Zhengyun]: "To make the speech of ancient and modern times mutually intelligible and to clarify the reasons for it." The [Qian Hanshu], 'Biography of Yang Xiong': "Xiong was fond of learning from youth; he did not make chapter-and-verse expositions, being content to have mastered the exegesis (訓詁) of the text." The [Jiu Tangshu], 'Jingji Zhi': "Exegetical glosses record the prognostications of the Six Classics — (the passage breaks off here)."
诃: To speak loudly in anger; to rebuke. The [Guangyun]: "To reprimand." The [Zhengyun]: "To censure." The [Hou Hanshu], 'Wenyuan Zhuan': "Mi Heng's speech was not compliant, and Huang Zu, ashamed, thereupon shouted at him." The [Shu Zhi], 'Biography of Liao Li': "Following the great general, he slandered and ridiculed (譏訶)." The [Beishi], 'Biography of Zhang Yao': "To encourage oneself in gentle inquiry, not wishing to berate the ancients for their faults."
评: No source text is recorded for this entry. Structurally it is a left-right phono-semantic compound (形声).
诅: To curse, to swear an oath. The [Guangyun]: "A curse, an imprecation." The [Shujing], 'Wuyi': "Their mouths cursed and blessed." The sub-commentary: "Cursing and blessing means to inform the spirits and ask them to send down calamity: to inform the gods with words is 祝 (to bless), to ask the gods to add calamity is 詛 (to curse)." The [Shijing], 'Xiaoya': "Bringing out these three things, we swear at you thus." The Explanation of Terms: "To bind one another with words of calamity and blessing is 詛." The [Zhouli], 'Chunguan': "The officer of curses is in charge of the invocation-formulas of oaths and curses." The commentary: "詛 means to bless so as to cause failure; great matters are called 盟, small matters 詛." The sub-commentary: "A 盟 binds the future; a 詛 curses the past." The [Hou Hanshu], 'Biography of Zhongchang Tong': "Cursing in the heart while reviling in the belly."
识: Constant; another account says "to know." The [Changjian]: "Glossing it as 常 has no sense." The [Yupian]: "識 means to recognize." The [Zengyun]: "To be able to distinguish and recognize."
诈: To deceive, to cheat. The [Erya], 'Shi Gu': "False." The [Zhengyun]: "Crafty and cunning." The [Zuo Zhuan], fifteenth year of Duke Xuan: "We will not deceive you, and you will not impose on us." The [Liji], 'Yueji': "The knowing deceive the stupid." The sub-commentary: "It means to cheat and deceive the stupid." The [Zhouli], 'Diguan, Sishi': "By means of the merchants he suppresses falsity and removes deceit." The sub-commentary: "He causes the falsity of goods to be prohibited and removes the deceit and emptiness of men." The [Jinshu] — (the passage breaks off here).
诉: To tell, to inform. The [Yupian]: "To state; to tell of a wrong." The [Guangyun]: "To defame." The [Zuo Zhuan], sixteenth year of Duke Cheng: "Xi Chou complained of the duke to the Marquis of Jin." The commentary: "To slander." The [Shiji], 'Guice Zhuan': "The king has virtue and rightness, and therefore has come to tell you."
诊: To examine, to look at. The [Yupian]: "To verify." The [Hou Hanshu], 'Biography of Wang Qiao': "An edict ordered the imperial physicians to examine and look at him." The commentary: "診 is also to look at." The [Zhuangzi], 'Renjian Shi': "The carpenter Shi woke and examined (診) his dream." The commentary: "To divine and verify."
诋: To censure harshly; another account says to shout at. The [Guangya]: "To slander." The [Yupian]: "Law; to revile." The [Zhengyun]: "To expose." The [Shiji], 'Biography of Ji An': "The clerks of the brush and knife specialized in deep and artful censure, entrapping people in crime." The [Qian Hanshu], 'Annals of Emperor Ai': "He abolished the laws against slander, defamation, and false accusation." Shigu's commentary: "詆 means to accuse falsely."
诌: Structurally a left-right phono-semantic compound (形声). [note: source text partially corrupted]
词: What is within as meaning and outside as words. The [Shiming]: "It is 嗣 (to continue); one composes fair words so that they succeed one another." The [Guangyun]: "To speak of." The [Zhengyun]: "Words." The [Zihui]: "Writing." The [Gongyang Zhuan], eleventh year of Duke Zhao: "The Chunqiu is a faithful record; as for its wording (詞), Qiu is the one at fault." The [Shiji], 'Rulin Zhuan': "At this time the Son of Heaven was fond of polished writing (文詞)." The [Jinshu], 'Biography of Guo Pu': "Pu's lyrics and rhapsodies were the finest of the restoration." The [Jiu Tangshu], 'Biography of Zhang Jiuling': "Zhang Yue often said to people: 'He is the foremost of the writers of our time.'"
诎: Structurally a left-right phono-semantic compound (形声). [note: source text partially corrupted]
诏: To tell, to inform. The [Erya], 'Shi Gu': "To guide." The commentary: "To teach and guide." Again: "To encourage." The commentary: "To aid and encourage." The sub-commentary: "To teach and guide is the same as to aid and encourage." The [Yunhui]: "詔 is a term used both by superiors and by inferiors." The [Zuo Zhuan], second year of Duke Cheng: "Luan Bo said: 'It was Xie's instruction (詔); what strength of mine had I in it?'" The commentary: "To inform." The [Zhouli], 'Tianguan, Dazai': "By the eight handles he instructed the king in controlling the hosts of officials." The commentary: "To inform, to assist." The [Zhuangzi], 'Daozhi' chapter: "One who is a father must be able to instruct (詔) his son." Ru Chun's commentary: "To teach."
译: Structurally a left-right phono-semantic compound (形声). [note: source text partially corrupted]
诒: To deceive one another; another account says to present, to bequeath. The [Shijing], 'Bei Feng': "I have brought this obstruction on myself." The commentary: "To bequeath." The [Zuo Zhuan], sixth year of Duke Zhao: "Shu Xiang sent a letter to Zichan." The commentary: "To present." The [Guangyun]: "Words of a parting gift."
诓: No source text is recorded for this entry. The character is a left-right phono-semantic compound (形声).
诔: A posthumous eulogy. The [Shiming]: "It is 累 (to accumulate): to accumulate and set out a person's deeds and praise them." The [Guangyun]: "It is 壘; to pile up and recount the merits and virtues of the deceased." The [Zhouli], 'Chunguan, Dazhu': "He made six forms of speech to reach between high and low, distant and near; the sixth is the 誄." The commentary: "It means to accumulate the virtues of the deceased's lifetime and confer the name, chiefly by composing the words for it." The [Zuo Zhuan], sixteenth year of Duke Ai: "When Confucius died, the duke eulogized him. Zi Gan said: 'He could not employ him in life, and now he eulogizes him in death — this is not in accordance with the rites.'" The [Liji], 'Tangong': "When Duke Zhuang of Lu and the men of Song fought at Chengqiu, the horses shied and the lines broke, and Xian Benfu and Pu Guo died. The duke said: 'It was not their fault.' Thereupon he eulogized them. Eulogies for ordinary officers began from this."
试: To use; to try. The [Guangya]: "To taste, to try." The [Zengyun]: "To probe; to compare." The [Yijing], 'Wuwang': "A medicine for no illness is not to be tried." The Explanation of Terms: "To test; one account says to use." The commentary: "試 means to taste a little of it." The [Shujing], 'Shundian': "He clearly tested them by their works." The [Liji], 'Ziyi' — (the passage breaks off here).
诖: To err; to deceive. The [Guangya]: "To cheat." The [Shiji], 'Biography of Liu Pi, King of Wu': "To throw the world into disorder (詿亂)." The [Qian Hanshu], 'Biography of Wang Mang': "Your servant Mang ought to receive the punishment for deceiving the throne and misleading the court." The [Jiyun] says it is sometimes written — (the passage breaks off here).
诗: The intent, the will. The [Shiming]: "It is 之 (to go): the going forth of the intent." The [Shujing], 'Shundian': "Poetry speaks the intent." The commentary: "What the mind goes out to is called the intent; when the mind has something to which it goes, it must take form in words — hence 'poetry speaks the intent.'" The [Shijing], 'Guofeng, Guanju' preface: "In the mind it is the intent; issued in speech it is poetry." The [Qian Hanshu], 'Yiwenzhi': "To chant his words is called poetry." The [Jiu Tangshu], 'Jingji Zhi': "Poetry is to record prosperity and decline and to chant joy."
诘: To question; to reprove, to censure. The [Guangya]: "To reprove, to blame." The [Yupian]: "To regulate, to reprimand, to ask about a crime." The [Shujing], 'Lizheng': "They could put their weapons and soldiers in order (詰)." The commentary: "To regulate." The [Liji], 'Yueling': "To interrogate and punish the violent and insolent." The commentary: "It means to ask about their crimes and prosecute them thoroughly." The [Laozi], Daodejing: "These three cannot be pressed to an answer." The commentary: "To question." The [Shiji], 'Biography of the Marquis of Pingjin': "Ji An questioned Hong in the court." The commentary: "To reprove and reproach."
诙: Structurally a left-right phono-semantic compound (形声). [note: source text partially corrupted]
诚: Sincerity, truthfulness. The [Guangya]: "Reverence." The [Zengyun]: "Pure, without falsity, genuine and true." The [Yijing], 'Qian' hexagram: "He guards against evil and preserves his sincerity." The sub-commentary: "It means that in guarding against evil and wickedness one should preserve one's own sincerity and truth." The [Shujing], 'Tai Jia': "The spirits and ghosts do not constantly enjoy offerings; they enjoy the sincere." The commentary: "It means that the spirits and ghosts are not tied to any one person: those who can be sincere and faithful have their sacrifices enjoyed." Zhen Dexiu says: "In the Tang and Yu ages there was no character 誠; the 'sincerity and fullness' of the [Shundian] is the meaning of 誠, which first appears when Yi Yin addresses Tai Jia." The [Liji], 'Yueji': "To make sincerity manifest and remove falsity is the warp of the rites." The [Zhongyong]: "Sincerity is the way of heaven; to make oneself sincere is the way of man." The commentary: "Sincerity means being true and without deception."
诛: To punish, to put to death. The [Guangya]: "To kill." The [Shujing], 'Yin Zheng': "Thus offending against the punishments of the former kings." The [Liji], 'Yueling': "To interrogate and punish the violent and insolent." The commentary: "誅 means to put the person to death." The [Qian Hanshu] — (the passage breaks off here).
诜: To offer words; Xu says: "To first offer one's words." The [Guangya]: "To ask." The [Guangyun]: "The words of many people." The source classifies the character as a phonetic loan (假借).
话: Words that meet and join in what is good. The [Erya], 'Shi Gu': "Words, speech." The sub-commentary, citing Sun Yan: "The words of a good man." The [Guangyun]: "Speech and talk." The [Shujing], 'Pangeng': "Then he spoke to the people who would not follow, and made a great announcement in sincerity." The commentary: "To tell, to speak." The [Shijing], 'Daya': "Be careful of your speech." The commentary: "Good words." The [Zuo Zhuan], sixth year of Duke Wen: "He set them down in fine sayings." The commentary: "He made fine sayings as a legacy of admonition."
诞: Boastful words. Xu says: "To recklessly make great claims." The [Guangyun]: "To deceive." The [Shujing], 'Wuyi': "Then they indulge and are vulgar and boastful." Cai's commentary: "Wild and false." Kong's commentary: "Deceitful and boastful." The [Shiji], 'Biography of Bian Que': "Master, may it not be that you are deceiving us?" The [Xunzi], 'Xiushen': "To speak lightly is called 誕." The [Shuoyuan], 'Zunxian': "Those whose mouths are sharp are mostly boastful and rarely trustworthy."
诟: 謑詬 is shame. The [Guangya]: "To revile." The [Yupian]: "Shame and disgrace." The [Guangyun]: "Anger." The [Zengyun]: "To abuse." The [Zuo Zhuan], eighth year of Duke Ai: "The men of Cao reviled him, and he did not go." Du's commentary: "To abuse and disgrace." The [Liji], 'Ruxing': "They constantly use the Confucians as a term of reproach and shame." The commentary: "詬病 is like shame and disgrace." The [Hou Hanshu], 'Biography of Deng Yu': "Kang heard of it and reviled him." The commentary: "To curse." The [Tangshu], 'Biography of Liu Wenjing': "Junya reviled him, saying, 'A rebel wants to kill me!'"
诠: To set out fully. The [Yupian]: "The substance of order and disorder." The [Guangyun]: "To level, to weigh." The [Leipian]: "To choose words."
诡: To reprove; to hold oneself responsible. The [Qian Hanshu], 'Biography of Jing Fang': "Your servant, sent out to guard a province, made himself responsible for achieving merit." Shigu's commentary: "He took it as his own burden of responsibility." Kong Rong's 'Memorial Recommending Mi Heng': "Formerly Jia Yi sought to be tried in a border commandery, making himself responsible for binding the Xiongnu chanyu." The commentary: "He reproached himself, undertaking to bind the chanyu."
询: To consult, to plan. The [Yupian]: "To ask." The [Shujing], 'Shundian': "He consulted on affairs and examined words." The [Shijing], 'Xiaoya': "Everywhere he goes he consults." The commentary: "Consultation among relatives is 詢." The [Zuo Zhuan], fourth year of Duke Xiang: "To consult one's relatives is 詢."
诣: Structurally a left-right phono-semantic compound (形声). [note: source text partially corrupted]
诤: To stop, to remonstrate. The [Yunhui]: "It means to stop a person's error." The [Zhengyun]: "To remonstrate and correct." The [Qian Hanshu], 'Biography of Wang Bao': "His remonstrances were immediately heeded." The [Shuoyuan], 'Chen Shu': "One who can speak his whole mind to his ruler, so that if used he may live and if not used he may die, is called 諍."
该: Structurally a left-right phono-semantic compound (形声). [note: source text partially corrupted]
详: To deliberate carefully, to examine. The [Yupian]: "To examine, to discuss, to be clear." The [Zengyun]: "Words complete." The [Shujing], 'Cai Zhong zhi Ming': "Examine carefully your seeing and hearing." The commentary: "To scrutinize." The [Shijing], 'Wei Feng': "The words of the inner chamber cannot be told in full." The commentary: "To speak of fully." The [Guliang Zhuan], twenty-ninth year of Duke Xiang: "He sets out the matter in detail (詳), honoring Bo Ji." The [Shiji], 'Fengshan Shu': "Its details cannot be recorded and heard." The [Qian Hanshu], 'Rulin Zhuan': "He widely summoned the learned men of the world." The commentary: "詳 means all, complete."
诧: Structurally a left-right phono-semantic compound (形声). [note: source text partially corrupted]
诨: No source text is recorded for this entry. The character is a left-right phono-semantic compound (形声).
诩: Great words. The [Yupian]: "The speech of people." The [Guangyun]: "Harmonious, universal, pervasive, great." The [Liji], 'Liqi': "His virtue was displayed and spread over all things (詡萬物)." The sub-commentary: "It means that when a king embraces the four seas he should display his virtue and make it pervade all things." The [Qian Hanshu], 'Biography of Yang Xiong': "He esteemed great luxury, and his beauties were exaggerated and grand." The commentary: "詡 means great."
诫: To admonish, to charge. The [Yupian]: "To command, to tell." The [Guangyun]: "Words of warning." The [Zengyun]: "Words that warn and admonish are called 誡." The [Yijing], 'Bi' hexagram: "The people of the town do not admonish."
诬: To add to, to impute falsely. Xu says: "To make what is not into what is." The [Yupian]: "To deceive and delude." The [Guangyun]: "誣 is to wrong." The [Zhengyun]: "To cheat, to smirch, to slander." The [Yijing], 'Xici': "The words of one who slanders the good wander." The sub-commentary: "One who falsely accuses good people has words that are empty and vague." The [Liji], 'Biaoji': "Therefore his receipt of emolument was not false." The commentary: "What is not trustworthy is called 誣." The [Guoyu], 'Zhou Yu': "Its — (the passage breaks off here)."
语: To discuss. Xu says: "Discussion and objection is 語; 語 is 午, for speech crosses (交午) with another. My words are 語; 吾 is a particle of speech. 言 is a straightforward statement; 語 is an answering response." The [Shiming]: "It is 敘 (to set forth), to set forth what one wishes to say." The [Yijing], 'Yi' hexagram: "The gentleman is careful in speech and discourse and temperate in eating and drinking." The [Shijing], 'Daya': "Here they speak, there they talk." The sub-commentary: "A straightforward statement is 言, a man speaking by himself; an answer to a difficulty is 語, two men facing one another." The [Liji], 'Zaji': "In the three years' mourning one may speak (言) but not converse (語)." The commentary: "言 is to speak of one's own affairs; 語 is to discuss and explain for others." The [Jiayu]: "When Confucius went to Tan he met Master Cheng on the road, and leaning their carriage canopies together they conversed all day."
诮: An ancient form of 譙 (to reproach). The [Shujing], 'Jin Teng': "The king also did not venture to reproach the Duke." The commentary: "To reprove." The [Qian Hanshu], 'Biography of Qing Bu': "King Xiang repeatedly sent envoys to reproach and summon Bu." The commentary: "誚 is to reprove."
误: An error, a mistake. The [Shujing], 'Lizheng': "Do not err in the various prisons and various careful matters." The commentary: "誤 is a fault." The [Liji], 'Pinyi': "If an envoy errs in his mission, the host ruler does not entertain him in person." The commentary: "誤 means an error in the ritual formalities." The [Qian Hanshu], 'Biography of Zhang Er': "How mistaken your words are!" The [Wu Zhi], 'Biography of Zhou Yu': "Yu was skilled in music; even after three cups of wine, if there were a flaw or error in the music he was sure to notice it. Hence the people of the time said, 'When the tune errs, Lord Zhou looks.'"
诰: To announce, to proclaim. Xu says: "To announce and make known by means of written words." The [Guangya]: "To teach." The [Yijing], 'Gou' hexagram: "The sovereign accordingly issued commands and proclaimed them to the four quarters." The [Zhouli], 'Chunguan': "The Grand Invocator made six forms of speech to reach between high and low, near and far; the third is the 誥." The commentary: "Du Zichun says that 誥 should be 告, and that documents may also be 告."
诱: To draw on by calls, to lure. The [Yupian]: "誘 means to lead." The [Zuo Zhuan], tenth year of Duke Xi: "Xi Rui said: 'Heavy gifts and sweet words are meant to lure me.'" The [Shiji], 'Shijia of Goujian, King of Yue': "The Wu grand steward Pi was greedy and could be lured with profit."
诲: To instruct, to teach. Xu [Xuan] explains it as 'to admonish repeatedly, as if dispelling obscurity.' [Yupian] glosses it 'to teach and display,' and [Guangyun] 'to teach and admonish.' [Yijing, Xici] warns that 'careless keeping teaches theft, and a pretty face teaches lewdness,' while [Shangshu, Yue Ming] speaks of 'receiving admonitions morning and evening, to aid my virtue.' Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
诳: To deceive, to delude. [Yupian] gives 'to mislead.' [Liji, Quli] says that a young child should always be watched lest he be deceived. The Shiji (Annals of the Gaozu) tells of Ji Xin riding in the king's carriage and posing as the King of Han in order to deceive the Chu army, and the Jiu Tangshu notes men 'deceiving one another by turns.' Left-middle-right in form, phono-semantic.
说: To explain, to expound; one account takes it as 'to talk, to converse.' [Shiming] derives it from 'to recount,' that is, to set forth in order. [Guangya] gives 'to discuss,' [Yupian] 'to speak,' [Guangyun] 'to tell,' and [Zengyun] 'to explain, to instruct.' Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
诵: To recite, to intone. Xu [Kai] says: 'To recite before a text; 誦 (sòng) takes after 從 (cóng, to follow), the mouth following its text.' [Guangyun] gives 'to read aloud and recite.' The [Zhouli, Chunguan, Dasiyue] lists among the arts taught to the sons of the state 'arousing, guiding, intoning, reciting, speaking and conversing,' the note distinguishing 'chanting from memory' as 諷 (fěng) from 'measured delivery in a voice' as 誦. The Shiji (Yilin) records that Ni Kuan always carried a classic with him and recited it whenever he rested. Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
诶: An exclamation of disgust or repugnance; one account reads it as 誒然 (xī rán), a manner of utterance. The Spring and Autumn tradition is cited for the phrase '誒誒出出,' which now appears in the [Zuo Zhuan], Duke Xiang, year 30, written with the character 譆. Left-right in form, compound ideograph.
请: To request, to ask; to beg leave. [Guangya] gives 'to seek,' [Yupian] 'to beg, to inquire,' [Zengyun] 'to pray for, to entreat.' [Shangshu, Tang Gao] has 'thereby to beg life for your multitude,' and the [Zuo Zhuan], Duke Xi, year 10, 'I have obtained my request from the Lord on High.' [Liji, Quli] prescribes that one rise when asking about one's studies and when asking for further instruction. Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
诸: To dispute, to discriminate; Xu [Kai] calls it 'a term of distinction.' [Erya, Shixun] explains the expressions 諸諸 and 便便 as 'disputatious,' the commentary adding that both describe fluency in argument. Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
诹: To consult together, to deliberate. [Erya, Shigu] gives 'to plan'; [Yupian] 'to inquire about affairs of government.' The Shijing (Xiaoya) has 'everywhere he consults,' and the [Zuo Zhuan], Duke Xiang, year 4, defines 'consulting on affairs' as 諏. The [Yili, Tesheng Kuishi Li] notes that no day was fixed by consultation. Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
诺: To answer, to assent. [Yupian] gives 'to reply,' [Zhengyun] 'an answering sound.' The Shijing (Lusong) has 'none dared not assent,' glossed in the commentary as 'a word of response.' [Liji, Yuzao] notes that when a father calls, one answers 唯 (wéi) and not 諾 (nuò), the commentary explaining that 唯 is quick and respectful while 諾 is slow and offhand. Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
读: To recite a text aloud. Xu Kai says: '讀 (dú) is like 瀆 (dú, to channel), as the four channels draw off water.' The Shijing (Yongfeng) says that 'words spoken within the inner chamber cannot be read aloud,' where the Mao commentary glosses 'to draw out,' the Zheng commentary adds that to draw out is to bring forth, and Zhu Xi takes it as 'to recite the words.' [Liji, Wen Wang Shizi] records that in winter one reads books and the scribe in charge of documents instructs one in them. Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
诼: No annotation survives in the source for this entry. The character is left-right in form and phono-semantic in structure.
诽: To slander, to defame. [Boya] gives 'to revile.' The Shiji (Annals of the Gaozu) notes that 'those who slander are executed with their kin'; the Zhuangzi (Keyi) speaks of 'lofty talk and resentful slander'; and the Zhanguoce observes that a state must have both slander and praise, the loyal minister contriving that the slander fall upon himself and the praise upon his ruler. Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
课: To test, to examine, to assess. [Guangya] gives 'to grade'; [Yupian] 'to deliberate'; [Zengyun] 'to reckon, to measure out.' The Shiji (Xiongnu) records the assessing of men and livestock, and the Hanshu (Jing Fang) a memorial on the method of examining merit and testing officials. The Jinshu (Yuandi) speaks of encouraging and assessing farming and sericulture, the Songshu (Shen Yue) of lightening the work quotas, and the Guanzi of a finished vessel that, untested, is neither used nor stored. Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
诿: To implicate, to shift a burden onto another; it appears in the compound 諈諉 (zhuì wěi), for which see the note under 諈 above. The Hanshu (Hu Jian) says the officer in charge 'does not shift the matter onto his superior,' Yan Shigu explaining that one who holds office should act as soon as he sees the law and must not burden his superior with the affair; the Tangshu (Cen Xi) asks why a man of real ability should be bound by such shifting. Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
谀: To flatter, to fawn. [Shangshu, Jiong Ming] warns that 'if the servant ministers flatter, their lord will think himself a sage'; the Shiji (Shusun Tong) records the reproach 'why, sir, are your words so flattering?'; the Zhuangzi (Yufu) defines flattery as 'to speak without choosing between right and wrong'; the Xunzi (Xiushen) as 'to agree with others in what is not good'; and the Yantielun notes that 'wealth and honour breed much flattering speech.' Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
谁: Who? [Yupian] explains it as 'not knowing the name.' The [Yijing, Tongren] is also cited, with the line 'going out of the gate, he is with others,' though the quotation as transmitted does not itself contain the character. Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
调: To harmonize, to blend. [Yupian] gives 'to bring into accord.' The Shijing (Xiaoya) has 'the bow and arrows were already tuned,' and the [Liji, Yueling] records that in mid-summer the flutes and reed instruments are tuned. Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
谄: To flatter, to toady; identical with 讇 in abbreviated form. Xu [Kai] explains it as 'to sink into,' and one account distinguishes 'agreeing to a man's face' as 諛 (yú) from 'artful words' as 諂 (chǎn). [Yijing, Xici] says 'the gentleman does not flatter in his dealings with superiors'; the [Zuo Zhuan], Duke Xiang, year 3, praises one who did not flatter even his enemy; the Lunyu has 'poor yet not flattering'; and the Shiji (Pingzhun Shu) describes 'flattering and fawning to win favour,' the Zhuangzi (Yufu) defining flattery as 'anticipating another's intent and speaking accordingly.' Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
谅: Sincere, trustworthy, true. The Shijing (Xiaoya) has 'you do not truly know me,' which the Zheng commentary glosses 'sincere' and Zhu Xi 'genuine.' A further citation, from the [Liji, Neize], is cut off in the source. Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
谆: Earnest, repeated in instruction. [Zhengyun] gives 'repeated words of instruction.' The Shijing (Daya) has 'I instruct you earnestly,' which Zhu Xi explains as 'detailed and thorough,' and the Shiwen notes that 諄 is also written 訰. Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
谇: To reprove, to scold, to rail at. [Yupian] gives 'to curse'; [Zengyun] 'to ridicule, to revile.' The [Guoyu, Wuyu] relates that the King of Wu, returning from his attack on Qi, reproved Shen Xu. The citation from the Tangshu is cut off in the source. Left-right in form, compound ideograph.
谈: To speak, to converse. Xu [Kai] says that to talk is to speak with pleasure and delight; [Guangyun] gives 'conversation, discussion.' The [Gongyang Zhuan], Duke Min, year 2, notes that the men of Lu still regard a certain affair as 'a fine tale,' and the [Liji, Ruxing] holds that 'speech is the ornament of benevolence.' The Shiji (Huaji) praises talk that 'subtly hits the mark,' and the Jinshu calls Wang Yan 'the master of conversation of his day.' Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
谊: Left-right in form and a compound ideograph (会意) in structure. [note: source text partially corrupted]
谋: To plan, to devise, to scheme. Xu Shen defines it as 'deliberating over difficulties'; [Erya, Shiyan] gives 'mind,' with the note that planning and deliberation are carried out with the mind. [Guangya] gives 'to discuss,' [Yupian] 'to calculate,' and the Zihui 'to consult over difficulties and ponder troubles.' [Yijing, Song] says the gentleman plans the beginning of affairs before undertaking them; [Shangshu, Hongfan] makes 'cleverness produce planning,' glossed 'to measure'; the Shijing (Xiaoya) has 'everywhere he consults and plans'; and the [Zuo Zhuan], Duke Xuan, year 14, warns that 'the greedy will surely plot against others.' Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
谌: Sincere, true, trustworthy. [Erya, Shigu] gives 'sincere, true'; [Shangshu, Xian You Yi De] says 'Heaven is hard to trust, and its mandate is not constant,' the tradition reading 諶 as 'to trust'; the Chuci (Jiuzhang) has 'truly weak and hard to sustain,' glossed 'sincere.' Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
谍: A spy; espionage within an army. [Yupian] gives 'to watch, to lie in wait.' The [Zuo Zhuan], Duke Huan, year 12, relates that when the Chu army divided and crossed at Peng, the men of Luo sent Bojia to spy on them, the commentary glossing 諜 as 'to watch' and the subcommentary explaining it as pretending to be a man of the enemy state in order to enter their army and observe matters. Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
谎: No annotation survives in the source for this entry. The character is left-right in form and phono-semantic in structure.
谏: To remonstrate, to admonish a superior. Xu [Kai] explains it as 'to interpose': when what the ruler says is wrong, the minister offers what is right and thereby interposes; in the text 柬 (jiǎn) forms 諫, 柬 meaning to sort out much good and evil so as to correct the ruler. The passage is cut off in the source at this point. Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
谐: Left-right in form and phono-semantic in structure. [note: source text partially corrupted]
谑: To jest, to banter. [Erya, Shixun] with Guo's commentary gives 'to tease, to play.' The Shijing (Beifeng) has 'jesting and laughing wildly,' an image of unbridled mirth. Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
谓: To tell, to say, to call. Xu [Kai] explains that to call a thing so is to respond to it. [Guangya] gives 'to speak'; [Guangyun] 'to tell, to say'; [Zengyun] 'to speak with someone.' [Yijing, Qian] is cited for the interrogative 'what does it mean?', the subcommentary explaining that a hypothetical question is posed and so the phrase is used; the Shijing (Zhaonan) has 'wooing the many gentlemen, one tells them of it,' the tradition noting that a mere word would settle the agreement; and the [Zuo Zhuan], Duke Zhao, year 8, asks 'why not tell him of it?' Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
谔: Left-right in form and phono-semantic in structure. [note: source text partially corrupted]
谕: To announce, to proclaim, to make understood. [Leipian] gives 'to enlighten'; the Yunhui explains that where a man has not yet understood, one tells him so as to make him understand. The [Guliang Zhuan], Duke Huan, year 6, speaks of 'cultivating instruction and clearly proclaiming the way of the state'; [Liji, Jiyi] has 'making clear their intentions,' the subcommentary describing how the prayer officer announces and informs the spirits, making them understand by those intentions; and the [Zhouli, Qiuguan, Yashi] is cited for proclaiming the guilt of offenders. Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
谖: To deceive, to cheat. [Guangyun] gives 'to cheat.' The [Gongyang Zhuan], Duke Wen, year 3, asks why, if this was an attack on Chu, the record says he rescued Jiang, the answer being that it was a deception; the Hanshu (Xi Fu Gong) speaks of 'falsely concocting deceitful schemes.' Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
谗: To slander, to speak evil of another. [Yupian] gives 'artful flattery'; the Zhengzitong, 'to exalt and embroider evil words, ruining the good and harming the capable.' [Shangshu, Shundian] has 'I hate the words of slander that destroy conduct'; the Zhuangzi (Yufu) says 'to love telling others' faults is called slander'; the Xunzi (Xiushen) 'to injure the good is called slander'; and the Shuoyuan (Chenshu) 'he who obscures the good is the slanderer of the state.' Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
谘: No annotation survives in the source for this entry. The character is left-right in form and phono-semantic in structure.
谙: To know well, to be practised in. [Yupian] gives 'to know'; [Zengyun] 'to be practised in, to have gone through'; the Liushu Tong 'to have heard repeatedly'; the Zihui 'to understand.' The Hou Hanshu (Yu Yan) records a man who knew the very number of the trees and stumps in a tomb grove, and the Jinshu (Diao Xie) speaks of one long in the central court and practised in old matters. Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
谚: A saying, a proverb. [Guangyun] gives 'a vulgar saying.' [Shangshu, Wuyi] has 'then idleness and proverbial talk,' the tradition explaining that rustic sayings are called 諺; the [Zuo Zhuan], Duke Zhao, year 1, quotes a proverb that the old man will know it and dotage will overtake him. Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
谛: To examine closely, to scrutinise. [Shangshu, Hongfan], with Kong's commentary, has 'one must subtly examine'; the subcommentary explains that in listening one must distinguish right from wrong and must be subtle and exact in scrutiny. The Hou Hanshu (Jisi Zhi) remarks that the word 禘 means 諦, the careful ordering of the ancestral ranks. Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
谜: A riddle, an enigma; a hidden saying. The Yanfanlu notes that in antiquity there was no character 謎, and that what Wu Ju and Dongfang Shuo called 'concealments' was this same device, riddles proper appearing by the time of the Bao Zhao collection. The Wenxin Diaolong observes that from the Wei dynasty onward gentlemen transformed the jester's art into riddles, a riddle being a turning and twisting of words so as to confuse the hearer. Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
谝: Left-right in form and phono-semantic in structure. [note: source text partially corrupted]
谟: Counsel, plan, deliberation. Xu [Kai] distinguishes them: to consider one matter and draw up one plan is 謀 (planning), while to discuss at large and be about to settle the plan is 謨. The Shangshu contains the 'Great Yu's Counsel' and 'Gao Yao's Counsel,' the tradition explaining that 謨 means plan, Great Yu having planned the nine services and Gao Yao the nine virtues. The Shijing (Daya) has 'great plans fix the mandate,' and the [Zhouli, Qiuguan, Daxingren] is cited in connection with the summer audience. Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
谠: Straightforward speech, honest words. [Yupian] gives 'good words.' The Hanshu (Ban Gu Xuzhuan) has 'I have long not seen Master Ban; today I hear upright words again,' and the Wei Zhi (Wang Xiu) laments that loyal and upright speech was not made manifest in the times. Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
谡: No annotation survives in the source for this entry. The character is left-right in form and phono-semantic in structure.
谢: To take leave, to depart; to decline. [Guangya] gives 'to depart.' The Chuci (Jiuzhang) has 'I would have the year take its leave with my long friend,' the note glossing 謝 as 'to leave.' Left-middle-right in form, phono-semantic.
谣: Left-right in form and phono-semantic in structure. [note: source text partially corrupted]
谤: To slander, to censure. [Guangya] gives 'to hate, to detest'; [Yupian] 'to slander, to match, men speaking of his evil'; [Zengyun] 'to revile.' The [Zuo Zhuan], Duke Zhuang, year 22, has a sojourning subject beg not to disgrace a high office and thereby hasten official censure; the Shiji (Xiaowen) records that at court there were a banner for advancing the good and a board for criticism; and the Zhanguoce tells how Yue Yang, returning to speak of his merit, was shown by the Marquis of Wen a chest full of letters of censure. Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
谥: 謚 (posthumous name): the trace of a man's conduct, composed of 言 (speech) with 益 (yì) as phonetic. The [Wujing Wenzi] cites 謚 as the form given in the Shuowen. Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
谦: Humble, modest. [Yupian] gives 'to yield'; [Zengyun] 'to offer respect, not to be full of oneself.' Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
谨: Careful, attentive, respectful. [Yupian] gives 'respectful'; [Guangyun] 'pure, undefiled'; [Zengyun] 'cautious, single-minded, weighty.' [Yijing, Qian] has 'careful in ordinary conduct'; [Shangshu, Pangeng] 'reverently careful of Heaven's mandate'; the Shijing (Daya) 'so as to be careful with the bad'; the [Liji, Yueling] 'in the first month of winter the king orders the hundred officials to be careful in covering and storing'; the Shiji (Wan Shijun) describes a chancellor merely honest and careful; and the Hanshu (Li Yiji) observes that in great undertakings one is not meticulous about small carefulness. Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
谩: To deceive, to dupe. The Shiji (Qin Shihuang) describes men who 'cower below and submit to deceit, cheating to win favour.' The citation from the Jinshu is cut off in the source. Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
谪: Left-right in form and phono-semantic in structure. [note: source text partially corrupted]
谫: Left-right in form and phono-semantic in structure. [note: source text partially corrupted]
谬: Erroneous, false; literally 'the wild words of a madman.' [Boya] gives 'to err, to deceive'; [Yupian] 'to disorder, to cheat'; [Guangyun] 'a discrepancy.' [Shangshu, Jiong Ming] urges the ruler to correct transgressions and rectify errors and so reform his wrong mind; the Shiji (Li Si) speaks of falsifying doctrine and rejecting words; the Hanshu (Sima Qian) coins the proverb that a hair's breadth of difference leads to a thousand li of error; and the Shu Zhi (Xiang Lang) records a man who collated books with his own hand and corrected errors. Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
谭: No annotation survives in the source for this entry. The character is left-right in form and phono-semantic in structure.
谮: To slander secretly, to inform against. [Boya] gives 'to accuse falsely'; [Yupian] 'to slander'; the Yunhui, 'to enter from the side is called 譖.' The Shijing (Xiaoya) says that where there are slanderous words the man is pushed back, the note explaining that slanderers join to drive him out; the [Gongyang Zhuan], Duke Zhuang, year 1, records a lady slandering the duke to the Marquis of Qi, with the note that to state the facts is 訴 (to complain) while to add falsehood is 譖; and the Hanshu (Sun Bao) speaks of suffering wrongful slander. Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
谯: To reproach, to shout at, to blame. [Guangya] gives 'to shout at'; [Guangyun] 'to reprove'; [Zengyun] 'to reproach with words.' The Yangzi Fangyan records it as meaning 'to reprove' in Qi, Chu, Song, Wei and Jing. The passage is cut off in the source at this point. Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
谰: Falsely to accuse or deny; it appears in the compound 詆讕 (dǐ lán). [Yupian] explains it as heaping false words upon another. The Hanshu (Wen San Wang) records a king who, feigning illness, gave false and evasive statements, Yan Shigu glossing 讕 as 'to slander and to conceal.' Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
谱: A register, a genealogy, a table of lineage. [Guangya] gives 'a document'; [Yupian] 'a category'; the Shiming, 'to spread out,' that is, to spread out and display the matters recorded. The Wenxin Diaolong says that for governing the people at large there are genealogies, registers and records, and that 譜 (pǔ) means 普 (universal), for noting and ordering the succession of generations relies on completeness; the Shijing preface uses the term for the ordering of the Odes, Kong's subcommentary explaining that 譜 belongs to the category of the preface and was so named to avoid the title of Zixia's Preface while listing the succession of the feudal lords and the order of the poems. The Shiji (Sandai Shibiao) notes that before the Yin the feudal lords cannot be genealogised, the Hanshu records Liu Xin's Santong Li Pu, and the Jiu Tangshu (Jingji Zhi) states that genealogies record hereditary clans and their order of succession. Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
谲: Craft, cunning, deceit. A Yi-Liang gloss makes it 'to deceive the world with falsehood'; [Guangya] gives 'to deceive'; the Yangzi Fangyan records 'to cheat' as used east and west of the Pass. The Lunyu says that Duke Wen of Jin was crafty and not upright while Duke Huan of Qi was upright and not crafty, Zheng's note reading 'crafty' and Zhu Xi 'deceitful.' The Shiji (Sima Xiangru) speaks of marvellous and strange things, crafty and bizarre; the Hanshu (Wang Ji) of men who each took the expedient, craft and guile finding their own place; the Xunzi (Dalue) of those who flatter the jealous and benighted being called 'associated guile'; and the Han Feizi (Gufen) of ministers who use guile to delude their ruler and secure private ends, the note explaining the setting up of deceitful schemes to mislead him. Left-right in form, compound ideograph.
谳: Left-middle-right in form and phono-semantic in structure. [note: source text partially corrupted]
谴: To reprove, to censure, to blame. [Guangya] gives 'to blame'; [Guangyun] 'to be angry, to reprove'; [Zhengyun] 'to ridicule.' The Shijing (Xiaoya) has 'fearing this censure and wrath,' the tradition glossing it as blame for guilt; the Zhanguoce records a grand diviner censuring an affair, saying that the sacrificial land of Zhou had become a haunting. Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
谶: A prophecy, a portent, a book of prognostications. Xu [Kai] says that all 讖 and 緯 (apocryphal writings) speak of future verifications; the Liushu Gu calls them words of a foreordained omen; the Shiming derives the word from 'fine,' its meaning being fine and subtle. The Shiji (Zhao Shijia) tells of Gongsun Zhi writing and storing a prophecy, from which the prophecy of Qin came forth; the Hou Hanshu (Guangwu) records Li Tong and others of Wan persuading Guangwu by means of charts and prophecies, the note explaining 讖 as books of the mandate-tallies; and the Jinshu (Wudi) records that in the third year of Taishi the study of astrology, prophecy and apocrypha was prohibited. Left-right in form, compound ideograph.
豆: An ancient vessel for eating meat. [Erya, Shiqi] says that a wooden 豆 is called 豆. [Shangshu, Wucheng] has 'holding the 豆 and the sacrificial baskets'; the Shijing (Xiaoya) has 'the 豆 are very many'; and the [Gongyang Zhuan], Duke Huan, year 4, speaks of dried 豆 among the offerings, the note describing 豆 as a sacrificial vessel shaped like a lamp. The [Liji, Mingtang Wei] records that the Xia used the plain 楬豆, the Yin the jade 豆 and the Zhou the carved 獻豆, the note explaining that 楬 means without ornament and 獻 (read suō) means carved laterally. Pictographic in structure.
豇: No annotation survives in the source for this entry. The character is left-right in form and phono-semantic in structure.
豉: Salted, fermented beans. Xu [Kai] explains that 尗 (shū) is the bean and 幽 (yōu) means that it is made in a dark place. The Shiming derives 豉 from 'to relish,' since the five flavours must be harmonised with it before they can be relished. The Shiji (Huozhi) mentions a thousand measures of salt and beans, and the Hanshu (Shihuo) tells of Fan Shaoweng of Chang'an who sold fermented beans and was nicknamed Bean Fan. Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
豊: A vessel for performing rites. The [Liushu Zheng E] states that this was the ancient character for 禮 (rites), and that later men, finding it confusable with 豐 and holding rites weightier than sacrifices, added 示 (shì) to distinguish it; all characters such as 澧 and 醴 take it as their component. The Shuowen is cited for the original form, though the citation is cut off. Upper-lower in form, pictographic.
豌: The source for this entry is a modern dictionary extract rather than a classical annotation: 豌 (wān), as in 豌豆, the pea, an annual or biennial herbaceous plant bearing pods whose tender pods and seeds are edible, and the seed of that plant. The entry ends in page code. Left-right in form, phono-semantic in structure. [note: source text partially corrupted]
豎: To stand upright, to erect. Xu [Kai] explains that the character contains the bean-vessel and therefore means to set upright. The Hou Hanshu (Lingdi) records that a locust tree uprooted itself and stood upside down, and the Wei Zhi (Zhong Yao) speaks of raising the fallen and making them stand. Upper-lower in form, phono-semantic.
豐: The source preserves only a fragment, citing the Shuowen for the statement that 豊 is a vessel for performing rites, followed by the gloss that its original meaning was the tray for holding wine vessels in antiquity. Upper-lower in form, pictographic.
豔: Left-right in form and phono-semantic in structure. [note: source text partially corrupted]
豕: A pig, a boar. Xu Shen writes that it is the 彘, that it raises its tail and is therefore called 豕, and that it is depicted with bristles, feet and a tail behind, Xu [Kai] explaining that 竭 means 'to raise.' [Yupian] gives it as the general name for pig and boar, and the Yangzi Fangyan notes that east and west of the Pass the pig is sometimes called 彘 and sometimes 豕. The Lin shi Xiaoshuo derives the name from its eating unclean things; the Da Dai Liji (Yi Benming) assigns it to the fourth month because the seasons govern the pig; and the Bencao Gangmu (Li Shizhen) places it under Water among livestock, under Kan among the trigrams, and under the Shi constellation among the stars. [Yijing, Shuogua] has 'Kan is the pig,' and the Piya explains that Kan's nature tends downward and that the pig can lower its head. Pictographic.
豖: An indicative character (指事) in structure. [note: source text partially corrupted]
豚: A small pig, a piglet. The Xiao Erya says that the young of a pig is 豚. [Yijing, Zhongfu] has 'the pig-fish: auspicious,' Kong's subcommentary observing that the pig is the lowliest of beasts; the [Liji, Quli] prescribes that in the ancestral sacrifice the pig be called fat; and the [Zhouli, Tianguan, Paoren] records that in spring lamb and piglet are used with fragrant fat. Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
象: The elephant: long of trunk and tusk, a great beast of the southern Yue, bearing young once every three years, the character depicting the shape of ears, tusks and four feet. [Erya, Shidi] counts the rhinoceros and elephant of Mount Liang among the fine things of the south, the subcommentary explaining that these two beasts' hides, horns, tusks and bones are the finest of materials; the Shijing (Lusong) has 'the great tortoise and elephant ivory'; the [Zuo Zhuan], Duke Xiang, year 24, warns that the elephant has tusks and thereby burns its own body, for they are its valuables; and the [Liji, Yuzao] rules that the feudal lords use an ivory tablet while a common officer may use bamboo headed with ivory. Upper-lower in form, pictographic.
豢: To rear pigs in a pen on grain. [Guangyun] gives 'to raise livestock on grain.' The [Liji, Yueling] mentions fodder and rearing in mid-autumn, the note distinguishing the feeding of cattle and horses as 芻 from that of dogs and pigs as 豢, and the subcommentary adding that grass-eating is 芻 and grain-eating 豢. Upper-lower in form, compound ideograph.

The Shanhaijing records that on Mount Zhu there is a beast shaped like a piglet, with white hair, as large as a hairpin and black-tipped, called the 豪彘. The citation is cut off in the source. Upper-lower in form, phono-semantic.

豬: A pig: a boar with three bristles dwelling together. [Erya, Shishou] gives 豬 as the young of a pig, the note adding that it is also called 彘 and, in Jiangdong, 豨, all being common names; the Yangzi Fangyan records that between Wu and Yang it is called 豬子. The passage from the Piya is cut off in the source. Left-right in form, phono-semantic.

豳: The state of the Grand King of Zhou, at Meiyang in You Fufeng. Originally written 邠, composed of 邑 (yì) with 分 (fēn) as phonetic, it is also written 豳, the Meiyang postal station being its site; its people held night markets, and there is a Mount Bin. The Shijing (Daya) has 'Oh, Duke Liu, he lodged at Bin,' and the Shipu relates that Duke Liu, great-grandson of Hou Ji, moved from Tai to the land of the Rong and Di, the region later belonging to Xunyi in Fufeng. The entry goes on to trace the name's later history: the Southern Bin prefecture of the Northern Wei lost its 'Southern' under the Western Wei, and the Tang emperor Xuanzong, finding the character resemble 幽, changed it to 邠 in the Kaiyuan period. Half-enclosing in form, compound ideograph.
豹: A leopard: like a tiger with round markings. Lu Ji's commentary on the Shijing distinguishes the red leopard, red-haired with black markings, from the white leopard, white-haired with black markings; the Erya Yi notes that Tuzhou has black leopards, and the Dongming Ji that blue leopards come from the mountain of Langban with a colour like kingfisher blue. The Bencao Yanyi describes the earth leopard as small and wholly unmarked, while the Zhengzitong gives a fuller account: the leopard resembles a tiger but is smaller, white-faced, with red-yellow hair and black markings like coin-rings, five rings in the middle and four on each side, called the gold-coin leopard and fit for fur, one whose markings resemble mugwort leaves being called the mugwort-leaf leopard. Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
豺: The dhole, a kind of wolf. Yan Shigu's note to the Jijiu Pian describes it as deep-furred with dog's feet; the Zhengzitong gives it a long tail, white cheeks and yellow colour, and reports Lu Dian's saying that the common phrase 'thin as a 豺' arises because 豺 is homophonous with 柴 (firewood) and the animal's body is slender. The citation from the Shijing (Xiaoya) is cut off in the source. Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
豻: The 豻 (àn), also written with the dog radical as 犴. The Jiyun notes that it is alternatively written 貋, and that 犴 is the variant form of 豻. Left-right in form, classified as a loan character (假借).
貂: The sable: a kind of rat, large and yellow-black. The Hou Hanshu (Yufu Zhi) describes the military cap to which attendants and regular attendants added gold ornaments, a cicada motif and a sable tail as decoration; Ying Shao's note explains that the sable is inwardly fierce and outwardly mild, and Xu Guang's that its rich purple lustre is not glaringly bright, sable fur having first been used in the cold north to warm the forehead before being attached to the cap as an ornament. The Tangshu (Huihu) records that in dress the people prized sable and 豽. Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
貅: Left-middle-right in form and phono-semantic in structure. [note: source text partially corrupted]
貇: Left-right in form, classified as a loan character (假借). [note: source text partially corrupted]
貉: The northern 豸, a beast-name applied to the northern peoples. The [Wujing Wenzi] notes that in the classics 貉 is traditionally written 蠻貊, and the [Zhouli, Xiaguan, Zhifangshi] lists the four Yi, the eight Man, the seven Min and the nine Mo among the peoples of the outer regions. Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
貊: Left-right in form and a compound ideograph (会意) in structure. [note: source text partially corrupted]
貍: A crouching beast resembling the 貙, identified in the Zhengzitong as the wild cat, of which several kinds are described: those the size of a fox with mixed yellow-black hair and cat-like stripes; the round-headed, long-tailed cat-貍 that steals chickens and ducks; the tiger-貍, striped like a 貙-tiger with a square muzzle and pointed head, which eats insects, rats and fruit; the nine-jointed 貍, like the tiger-貍 but with alternating black-and-white coin-patterned tail, whose skin serves for fur collars; the fragrant 貍, leopard-marked and musk-scented, that is, the civet; and the white-faced, fox-tailed ox-tail 貍 of the south, also called the white-faced 貍. Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
貓: The cat: a kind of 貍, a beast that catches rats. [Guangyun] gives 'a beast, to catch rats'; the [Liji, Jiaotesheng] explains that the cat is welcomed at the sacrifices because it eats the field rats; and the Zhengzitong quotes Lu Dian to the effect that rats are good at harming young grain, and since the cat can catch rats its character takes 苗 (miáo, sprout) as its component. Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
貔: A kind of leopard, from the state of Mo. [Guangya] identifies it with the 貍貓; [Shangshu, Mushou] compares warriors to tigers and 貔, the tradition calling it otherwise 執夷 and assigning it to the tiger kind; and the Shijing (Daya) speaks of presenting its skins, Lu Ji's subcommentary noting that the 貔 resembles a tiger, or on some accounts a bear, and is called the white bear in Liaodong. Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
貘: The tapir: like a bear and yellow, from central Shu. The Zhengzitong reports that its teeth are the hardest of all, shattering iron hammered against them, and that fire cannot burn it, only antelope horn being able to break it. The Shenyi Jing tells of a southern beast with hair black as lacquer that eats iron and drinks water, called the iron-gnawer, and the Shiyi Ji of cunning hares on Mount Kunwu whose bellies were full of iron, from which swords were cast that cut jade like mud, all of the 貘 kind. Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
贝: A sea shellfish, the cowrie. In antiquity cowries served as currency and tortoise shells were treasured; the Zhou had coinage, and by the Qin cowries were abolished and money circulated. [Erya, Shiyu] distinguishes the cowries that dwell on land as 贆, those in water as 蜬, the large as 魧 and the small, in a passage cut off in the source. Pictographic.
负: To rely on, to bear. Xu Shen writes that it means to rely on and is composed of 人 (a man) guarding 貝 (cowries), meaning that he has something to rely upon. The Shiji (Wei Qi Wu'an Hou) records that Wu'an, relying on his high place, was fond of power. Upper-lower in form, compound ideograph.
贡: To present tribute; literally to offer merit. The [Shangshu, Yugong preface] relates that Yu divided the nine provinces, following the mountains and clearing the rivers, and made the tribute according to the soil, the tradition explaining that he fixed the grades of tribute by what each land produced. The [Zhouli, Tianguan, Dazai] has 'by the nine tributes bringing in the resources of the states,' and the [Liji, Quli] states that the five officials presenting tribute is called 享, the note adding that 貢 means 功 (merit). Upper-lower in form, phono-semantic.
财: Wealth, what men treasure. Xu [Kai] defines it as what can be brought into use; [Yupian] explains the term as grain for food, goods and gifts. [Yijing, Xici] asks by what one gathers men and answers 'by wealth,' the note adding that wealth is that by which things are supplied and produced; [Shangshu, Yugong] has 'carefully assess the wealth and taxes,' the tradition explaining that what is cared for is wealth, goods, tribute and taxes; and the [Zhouli, Tianguan, Dazai] speaks of collecting wealth and valuables by the nine levies, the note defining 財 as coin and grain, while the [Liji, Fangji] mentions wealth first and rites after, glossed there as silk and cloth. Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
责: To demand, to require, to hold to account. The [Zuo Zhuan], Duke Huan, year 13, says that Song made many demands for bribes upon Zheng. Upper-lower in form, phono-semantic.
贤: Worthy, able and good. Xu Shen defines it as 'of much ability'; [Yupian] as 'having good conduct.' [Yijing, Ding] has 'great success, by which the sages and worthies are nourished.' Upper-lower in form, phono-semantic.
败: To ruin, to defeat, to spoil. [Erya, Shiyan] gives 'to overturn'; the Shiming, 'to collapse, to be routed.' Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
账: No annotation survives in the source for this entry. The character is left-right in form and phono-semantic in structure.
货: Goods, merchandise, wealth. [Guangyun] explains that 貨 is 化 (to transform), goods being things that change and are exchanged, and so the character contains 化. [Yijing, Xici] describes markets held at midday, gathering the people and assembling the goods of the world, with trade and dispersal; [Shangshu, Hongfan] numbers goods second among the eight offices of government, the tradition defining them as treasures and useful things; and the [Zhouli, Tianguan, Dazai] speaks of merchants circulating goods and valuables, the note defining 貨 as metal and jade. The Hanshu (Shihuo Zhi) gives the fullest account: goods are cloth and silk that can be worn, together with gold, knife-money, tortoise shell and cowries, that by which wealth is divided, profit distributed, and have and have-not connected. Upper-lower in form, phono-semantic.
质: To pledge, to give a thing as surety. The [Zuo Zhuan], Duke Yin, year 3, records that Zhou and Zheng exchanged hostages. Half-enclosing in form, phono-semantic.
贩: A peddler: one who buys cheap and sells dear. The [Zhouli, Diguan, Sishi] describes the evening market, at which peddler men and peddler women are the principals, the note explaining that they buy in the morning and sell in the evening. The [Liji, Quli] insists that even a bearer or peddler must have someone he respects; the Shiji (Lü Buwei) records going back and forth to buy cheap and sell dear. The Jiyun notes a variant form, cut off in the source. Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
贪: To covet, to be greedy. The Shiming derives it from 探, to reach in, that is, to reach into another's share. The Shijing (Daya) says that the covetous man ruins his kind; the [Liji, Liyun] advises using men's benevolence and discarding their greed; and the Lisao of Qu Yuan laments that all contend to advance in greed, Wang Yi's note distinguishing loving wealth as 貪 from loving food as 婪. Upper-lower in form, phono-semantic.
贫: Poor, impoverished; literally wealth divided, hence little. [Erya, Shiyan] explains 寠 as poor, the note adding 'poor and mean' and the subcommentary that the poor are those without wealth. [Shangshu, Hongfan] numbers poverty fourth among the six extremes, the tradition explaining it as straitened in wealth; the Shijing (Beifeng) has 'in the end poor and needy'; and the Guoyu (Jinyu) tells of Han Xuanzi grieving over poverty while Shu Xiang congratulated him. Upper-lower in form, phono-semantic.
贬: To diminish, to lower, to censure. The [Gongyang Zhuan], Duke Yin, year 2, asks why the record withholds a clan name, the note explaining that it is a censure and that 貶 is like 損, 'to diminish.' Du Yu's preface to the Chunqiu observes that the classic serves for praise and blame by a single character. Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
购: To seek with wealth, to offer a reward for. Xu Shen defines it as seeking something by means of wealth. The Shiji (Han Shijia) says a ruler was about to go west to purchase help from Qin; the Hanshu (Gaodi) tells of using much gold to buy over Xi's generals, Yan Shigu explaining that 購 means to set a reward and enlist men. Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
贮: To store up, to lay by. [Yupian] gives 'to keep'; [Guangyun] 'to lodge.' The [Gongyang Zhuan], Duke Xi, year 3, notes the absence of stored grain, and the Hanshu (Shihuo Zhi) declares that storing up is the great destiny of the world. Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
贯: A string of coins; the Shuowen defines it as the string of coins and cowries. The Hanshu (Shihuo Zhi) records that the money of the capital piled up to hundreds of myriads, the strings rotting so that they could not be counted. Upper-lower in form, compound ideograph.
贰: Secondary, duplicate, a deputy. The [Shangshu, Zhouguan] has 'the second minister spread the transformation,' the tradition explaining 'as deputy to the three dukes'; the [Zhouli, Tianguan, Xiaozai] speaks of having charge of the duplicates of the six statutes, eight laws and eight rules of the state, the note defining 貳 as deputy; and the [Liji, Shaoyi] rules that riding in a secondary carriage one bows on the crossbar, the note explaining that the 貳 carriage is the deputy carriage. Half-enclosing in form, phono-semantic.
贱: Left-right in form and phono-semantic in structure. [note: source text partially corrupted]
贳: To lend, to let out on credit, to buy on credit. [Guangya] gives 'to buy on credit.' The Shiji (Gaozu) records that the founder often went to old Mrs. Wang and to Wu Fu to buy wine on credit, and the Hanshu (Shihuo) speaks of merchants and minor tradesmen who borrow and lend. Upper-lower in form, phono-semantic.

贵: Upper-lower in form and phono-semantic in structure. [note: source text partially corrupted]
贶: To bestow, to grant. [Guangyun] gives 'to give.' The Shijing (Xiaoya) has 'with all my heart I bestow it upon him,' and the [Yili, Shihun Li] says 'you, sir, have shown kindness and bestowed a wife upon so-and-so.' Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
贷: To lend, to grant, to give out. [Guangya] gives 'to give'; [Yupian] explains it as to lend, to lend in full, that is, to give a thing to another and later have its owner receive it back. The [Zhouli, Diguan, Quanfu] provides that for all who borrow, the office together with their officers distinguishes and grants the loan; the [Zuo Zhuan], Duke Wen, year 14, tells of a man who lent out his whole household's resources to the duke, his officers continuing the practice. Upper-lower in form, phono-semantic.

费: To spend, to expend, to waste wealth. Xu [Kai] explains that in this character wealth disperses like boiling water. The Lunyu says the gentleman is generous but not wasteful, He Yan's note adding 'without waste of wealth.' Upper-lower in form, phono-semantic.
贺: To congratulate, to bring congratulatory gifts. Xu Shen defines it as presenting congratulation with gifts; the Shijing (Daya) has 'from all quarters they came to congratulate'; the [Zhouli, Chunguan, Dazongbo] speaks of using the rites of congratulation to draw close states of different surname; and the [Liji, Jiaotesheng] notes that the wedding rite includes no congratulation, being concerned with the order of man. Upper-lower in form, compound ideograph.
贻: To present, to bequeath, to leave to. Xu Shen defines it as to give and to leave; in the classics it is generally used as 詒. [Erya, Shiyan] has '貽 is to leave,' the note explaining mutual giving; [Shangshu, Wuzi zhi Ge] has 'to leave to his descendants'; the Shijing (Beifeng) has 'she gave me a red tube,' the Shiwen noting that 貽 is also written 詒. Left-right in form, phono-semantic.

贾: A merchant; the Shuowen defines 賈 as the market, and one account as to sit and sell. The [Shangshu, Jiugao] tells of men who first led out ox-carts and went far to serve as traders; the Shijing (Beifeng) has 'the goods would not sell'; and the [Zhouli, Tianguan, Dazai] speaks of merchants circulating goods and valuables, the note distinguishing the travelling trader 商 from the settled 賈. Upper-lower in form, phono-semantic.
贿: Wealth, goods, valuables. [Erya, Shiyan] gives '賄, wealth,' the subcommentary noting it as the general name for goods and silk. The Shijing (Weifeng) has 'with my goods I moved away,' and the [Zhouli] again supplies the line about merchants circulating goods and valuables, the note there defining 賄 as cloth and silk. Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
赀: A small fine paid in goods to redeem oneself. Han law provided that a commoner who did not perform labour service paid twenty-two coins of 貲; Xu [Kai] notes that this is what in his day was a fixed levy. Upper-lower in form, phono-semantic.
赁: To hire, to rent, to work for hire. Xu Shen defines it as hire; [Yupian] as to borrow and hire; the Leipian as to hire a thing with wealth. The Shiji (Fan Ju) has 'I was hired out as a man's labourer.' Upper-lower in form, phono-semantic.

资: Resources, means, goods. Xu Shen defines it as goods. The [Yijing, Lü] has 'the traveller comes to the lodging and carries his resources,' the note explaining that he will surely obtain lodging and brings resources and goods with him. Upper-lower in form, phono-semantic.

赇: To bribe, that is, to bend the law by means of wealth and thereby give thanks. Xu [Kai] explains it as seeking something contrary to principle. The Shiji (Huaji) says of a magistrate that he fears the man has again taken bribes and bent the law. Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
赈: In classical usage, rich, abundant. [Erya, Shiyan] gives '賑, rich,' the note explaining abundantly rich and the subcommentary that such men are abundant in wealth. Zhang Heng's Xijing Fu has 'the villages are rich and abundant'; the Leipian notes that it is alternatively written 軫. Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
赉: To bestow, to give. [Erya, Shigu] gives '賚, to give.' The [Shangshu, Tangshi] has 'I will greatly bestow it upon you.' Upper-lower in form, phono-semantic.
赊: To buy or sell on credit. Xu Shen defines it as to buy on credit. The [Zhouli, Diguan, Sishi] speaks of using the Quanfu office to equalise goods and to collect and extend credit, the note explaining that where a buyer has no goods it is 賒, a sale on credit with the goods handed over. Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
赋: To levy, to tax; a tax. [Erya, Shiyan] gives '賦, to measure,' the note explaining that taxes are what assessment is made by; the Yangzi Fangyan gives '賦, to move,' the note explaining that levying taxes disturbs the people. The [Shangshu, Yugong] grades a region's tax as the highest, the highest, with occasional second, the tradition explaining 賦 as what the land produces, to be offered to the Son of Heaven; the [Zhouli, Tianguan, Dazai] numbers tribute among the eight rules for governing the capital regions, the note defining 賦 as a per-head levy paid in coin. The citation from the Hanshu is cut off in the source. Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
赌: To gamble, to wager. Xu Shen defines it as gaming with dice. [Boya] gives 'to take by gaming'; [Guangyun] 'to wager in sport.' The Jinshu (Xie An) tells of An and his brother's son gambling, the passage being cut off in the source. Left-right in form, phono-semantic.

赎: To redeem, to ransom. Xu Shen defines it as to exchange; [Yupian] as a pledge, that is, to extricate a man from guilt by means of wealth. The [Shangshu, Shundian] prescribes that gold serve as the redemption fine, though the citation is cut off in the source. Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
赏: Upper-lower in form and phono-semantic in structure. [note: source text partially corrupted]
赐: To bestow, to grant. [Pianhai] gives 'to grant'; the [Liji, Quli] rules that three bestowals do not extend to carriage and horses, the note explaining the three bestowals as the three appointments and the subcommentary adding that to receive an appointment is to receive a bestowal. Left-right in form, phono-semantic.
